1991.title: KeyMapper
1991.subTitle: Windows Control Panel Keyboard Utility Applet
1991.description: Former German rocker Mike Neumann was selling a Windows Multilingual Fonts package through an Arizona company named Data-Cal, and used a shareware Windows font creation utility of mine (this was before TrueType) to convert his fonts.  Mike contacted me, and got Data-Cal to hire me remotely to build a Control Panel applet that worked with his fonts.

1991.title: NoDOS
1991.subTitle: Windows Desktop Utility
1991.description: My second shareware program was called NoDOS, and it customized the Windows 3.0 Program Manager to display DOS programs like WordPerfect and Lotus 1-2-3 as different, customizable icons rather than them all displaying as the same gray 'DOS' icon when you switched out of them back into Windows. Data-Cal bought and packaged NoDOS from me and paid me a royalty for units sold through their catalog.
1991.postscript: This functionality ended up being built into Windows 3.1.

1992.title: The Yo Mama Snaps Program
1992.subTitle: Windows Desktop Utility
1992.description: The Yo Mama Snaps Program was a silly way to keep myself motivated to trudge through learning how to be a better C/C++ developer.  I took a set of jokes and made a little Windows 3.1 program that had scores of jokes available at the click of a button jokes that were both categorized and rated, so you could omit the more offensive ones from ever appearing as you wished.  The program is still described and downloadable from http://www.pimpdaddy.com/yomama/yomama-program.shtml

1992.title: GrpIcon
1992.subTitle: Windows Desktop Utility
1992.description: My third and final shareware program, GrpIcon (pronounced 'Group-Icon') picked up where NoDOS left off by customizing the Program Groups insode the Windows Program Manager, which was not built into Windows 3.1. GrpIcon was picked up by PC Magazine Editor Brian Livingston, and included in his book Windows Gizmos, which was sold in book stores and CompUSAs across the USA.  It also ended up in at least one other book, Shareware Icones from France, which showed up in the mail one day. Windows Gizmos printed the entire Help file verbatim, including inspirational acknowledgements that were not only unapologetically black, but controversial to many.  Nevertheless, over 2000 people registered GrpIcon at $20 each, so I quit my QA testing job that was paying me $43,000 a year and started doing my own thing full time.

1992.title: Inner-City Software
1992.subTitle: Brains in the 'Hood
1992.description: "Inner-City Software (code for Black Software Company) was established with the goal of 'Bringing Communities of Color into the Information Age,' and I sought out opportunities to create products and deliver technology services towards that objective. In 1992, the Boston Public Library published a book by Boston-area historian Robert Hayden titled 'African Americans in Boston: More Than 350 Years,' and a year or 2 later, I started negotiating with them to get the rights to digitize the text and images of the book as a searchable CD-ROM program, with the goal of giving it away to the Boston Public School system.

1994.title: Afro-Am Culture Forum
1994.subTitle: CompuServe Afro-Am Culture Forum: Software Section
1994.description: I moderated the Software section of American Visions Magazine's Afro-American Culture Forum on CompuServe in the early 90s.
1994.postscript: AACF and NetNoir were the first online spaces for people of color.

1995.title: African Americans in Boston: More Than 350 Years
1995.subTitle: CD-ROM Windows Desktop Educational Program
1995.description: "I reasoned that the most practical way to generate interest in the black community about technology was to create culturally relevant software.  My first idea for a black software product was a screen saver featuring photos and audio clips from Malcolm X, but after creating a prototype, I abandoned the idea because the size of audio files was too impractical to deliver via diskettes, and CDs were too expensive for just a screen saver, and I did not have any ideas on how to contact Malcolm’s family, nor knew anyone who I felt could negotiate use of the material without coming out of pocket for a product that was before its time and more to expose people to the idea of black software than something that any real market research would have found a market for.
1995.postscript: So I worked with the Boston Public Library to get the rights to digitally reproduce and distribute their 1992 book 'African Americans in Boston: More tThan 350 Years,' with the ultimate goal of getting it into the Boston Public School system so that children of color (and others) could grow up seeing black people represented in this new technology.

1995.title: Africana Libraries in the Information Age
1995.subTitle: Schomburg Center Presentation
1995.description: "In January 1995, I demonstrated the completed 'African Americans in Boston' CD-ROM product to an audience of librarians at the Schomburg Center or Research in Black Culture.  At this same event, Professor Henry Louis Gates presented a concept video of a black encyclopedia, that he ultimately partnered with Microsoft with to become 'Encarta Africana' and Africana.com, which existed in the late 90s to mid 00s.  Despite not having the resources of Harvard or Microsoft, I have ensured that the '350 Years' content is available to the world up to this very day, on Blackfacts.com.
1995.postscript: Yes, I made sure he knew what I was doing by meeting with him and showing him my completed product a month after the Schomburg event and expressing a desire to work with him on it, and yes, I am throwing shade.

1995.title: William Monroe Trotter Institute
1995.subTitle: Urban Think Tank in UMass Boston

1996.title: Blackside Productions
1996.subTitle: Creators of ‘Eyes On The Prize’
1996.description: For several years, Inner-City Software did Blackside's web sites that promoted their documentaries and the business operations they created behind some of them, like 'Breakthrough: The Changing Face of Science in America,' which featured scientists of color and had curricula products marketed to educational institutions.

1996.title: Boston Blacks Online
1996.subTitle: Over 6000 Stong, from Coast to Coast and More
1996.description: "Although email based, BBO was a precursor to social networks like Facebook, where active, and often spirited debate could be found any hour of the day or night.  While my view into BBO was that of the moderator (aka Usually Benevolent Dictator), I have been told that BBO was responsible for a variety of friendships and business deals, as well as a few marriages and babies, and in recent years, I have had several people I never met in person then come up to me and thank me for introducing them to the online world via BBO.

1996.title: Inner City Access
1996.subTitle: Urban Community Web Sites
1996.description: "By 1996, the Internet was making inroads from the nerdverse to the rest of the world, so I looked for all of the local black tech folks I could find, and asked them to help me collect information about local businesses and organizations and put Boston’s communities of color on the digital map at the Urls I registered at Roxbury.com, Dorchester.com and Mattapan.com.
1996.postscript:
"Inner-City Access Philosophy
We are socially conscious entrepreneurs working to improve our community’s social condition through the application of technology.
 
“Besides the obvious technology component of our annual projects, the common concept behind our efforts is the focus on interest above access, content above hardware. We have seen too much energy put into getting people access to computers without giving them reasons to care that they have this access. We know of too many computers that people already have access to (in all the Boston Public Libraries, for a local example) that are gathering dust because people have not been given enough good reasons to stretch out of their comfort zone and deal with this new, unfamiliar thing called a computer. 

We also have seen, all of our lives, that once a person desires something, s/he will find all sorts of ways to gain access to it, but if the desire is not there, access is meaningless. Therefore, our efforts to bring technology to the 'hood do not focus on how cool the technology is, but rather aim to show how the technology can be used as a tool to help people become better at whatever is important to them, give them more options, and ultimately improve their lives. By focusing on things that people are already interested in (like ourselves, our culture and history) and presenting the computer as a vehicle to find out more and feel better about ourselves, we are confident that we can help present the computer in a new and different light.”

-- Kenneth Granderson
President, Inner-City Software
"

1996.title: Million Man March Local Organizing Committee
1996.subTitle: Proposal to Connect the Local Organizing Committees Nationally
1996.description: The MMM Local Organizing Committees that formed after the 1995 Million Man March met on a quarterly basis in several locations across the country, and back in these days of expensive long distance phone costs, did not communicate much even at a regional level.  I proposed to connect the LOCs across the country for free by setting up email listservs and web sites for them.  I got my proposal as far as the Chicago Baptist minister who was running the organization, but I think that his lack of understanding of the idea (despite the pictures in the proposal) prevented him from understanding what a sea change this could have brought to activist communication across the nation.

1997.title: Black Facts Online
1997.subTitle: The Internet's First Black History Database
1997.description: Originally started as Inner-City Software's 1997 Black Community Technology Awareness project, Blackfacts.com is the world's first online Black History database and the only one that has been running continuously from its launch in February 1997 to the present day.  The #1 Google search result for 'black facts,' blackfacts.com has served hundreds of millions of Black Facts to millions of visitors across the globe.

1997.title: NSBE National Conference Presentation
1997.subTitle: VB For Fun And Profit
1997.description: Presentation I gave at the 1997 National Society of Black Engineers National Conference on using the Visual Basic programming language to build commercial or hobby application.  Gave away copies of VB valued at several hundred dollars that I got from Microsoft.

1997.title: Boston Vegetarian Society
1997.subTitle: Bringing Healthy Eating to the 'Hood
1997.description: While having been a vegetarian since the early 1990s, it has always been a personal choice rather than a major part of my identity or politics.  Nevertheless, as I had the fastest connection in the area and plenty of machines to spare, I hosted the Boston Vegetarian Society's web site for a while, and when they were looking for a new location for their annual Veggie Food Fest, recommended the Reggie Lewis Track Center in Roxbury, where the annual event has remained for over two decades.

1997.description: In these early years of personal computer usage growing in the home, I did this 'introduction to Computers' segment on Boston's CityLine program, which was the first time in Boston television history where black people discussed and informed the public about computers.

1997.title: Microsoft MVP Award
1997.subTitle: Probably the First Black Microsoft Most Valued Professional
1997.description: Awarded for helping the MS tech community with FrontPage, for which Microsoft purchased Vermeer Technologies for $160MM.  I had been using FrontPage for 2 years, for the Inner City Access Project and showed hundreds of folks how to use it to create cutting edge web pages.

1997.subTitle: Did Research on Online Communities

Congressional Black Caucus Foundation Web Site

1998.description: Another First, the New England Black Pages was the Internet's first Searchable Black Business Directory, which listed businesses in several New England states.

Boston Economic Development Organizations
2003.subTitle: Providing Funding for Companies that Didn't Need It
2003.description: CDC of Boston, Community Business Network, Mass Micro Enterprise Coalition, Minority, Micro Enterprise, Small Business in Mass, and Urban Initiative Fund. I replied that if I had kind of revenue, I would not have been looking for financing.
2003.postscript: I also asked if there were any businesses in urban Boston at the time at all that had that level of revenue, and never got an answer.

2013.subTitle: The offical web site of the Government of Saint Lucia
2013.description: The GOSL web site enables the Government of Saint Lucia to deliver timely and accurate information regarding government announcements, forms and national news to its 180,000 citizens.  Before the web site, residents would often risk 90-minute bus rides from one end of the island to the other to discover that a government office was closed that day.
2013.postscript: I am the sole architect, developer and support person for the site since its launch in 2013.

2017.title: Blackfacts.com Reboot
2017.subTitle: The World's #1 Black History Site, Conceived, Created, Coded and Powered by Black Expertise
2017.description: After two decades of Blackfacts running as a community information site, in collaboration with my longtime friend and business associate Dale Dowdie, we decided to evolve Blackfacts into a sustainable business that would grow into becoming The Black Wikipedia. So we gave it a face lift, found images for most of the Black Facts, linked the Black Facts with 2 Artifical Intelligence systems, and started building features like membership, commerce, special-interest virtual sites and educational applications to establish Blackfacts as not only the longest running and one of the Internet's most popular Black History sites, but a site that is uniquely qualified as being built on world-class technology built By Us, For Us, and 100% Owned By Us.
2017.postscript: If you want to find out about our educational or organizational products, affiliate programs, have products or services that you want to offer in our Wakanda Marketplace, or want to connect with us on other levels, please contact me at ken@blackfacts.com.

2019.description: Described as one of the 'Vanguard' of Black Technologists who helped lay the foundation for today's ubiquitous use of the Internet in today's black activism.
2019.postscript: While the book says that the Vanguard cashed out, gave up or moved on, I am still here and still creating world-class technology For Us, By Us.

We know, we know, this podcast is almost 2 hours. Don't worry it's well worth the listen, so sit back, grab a cup your favorite beverage and be ready to be inspired!
On this episode of the Blacks In Technology BIT Tech Talk podcast, Greg sits down with Ken Granderson and Dale Dowdie of Blackfacts, the Internet’s first Black History Encyclopedia, serving hundreds of millions of Black History facts to its global audience.
BlackFacts.com endeavors to become the premiere online repository of black culture both nationally and internationally. Dale and Ken are two brilliant tech pioneers who have been in the tech entrepreneurship game since it started.

2021.title: That's When I Knew Podcast
2021.subTitle: Podcast Interview
2021.description:
Founder & CTO of Blackfacts.com, Ken Granderson, joins us on That’s When I Knew for a casual chat around:
Growing up in the Bed-Stuy neighborhood of Brooklyn New York in the 70s/80s and not seeing many white-collar jobs.
Getting into MIT and discovering a passion for computer science/technology at an early age.
The inspiration behind starting Blackfacts, the first online encyclopedia for black history, and how they are building the technological infrastructure to capture information about black people wherever it's coming from and deliver it back in an organized and effective way.
Advice to younger black professionals: 'controlling the narrative', 'chasing your passion not money', 'doing work to push the culture forward' and several other gems from Ken's 25 year+ career journey.
https://www.twikpodcast.com/podcast/episode/4d287f44/203-controlling-the-narrative-with-ken-granderson

2021.title: 25 Years of Teching While Black
2021.subTitle: Presentation for The Future Is Now Conference
2021.description:
Blackfacts Founders Ken Granderson and Dale Dowdie discuss their unique history of 25 Years of being Unapologetically Black Technology Professionals and Entrepreneurs who have:
  • Created boxed software products
  • Written code for NASA
  • Sold software online since the early 90s
  • Created Educational Software on Black History since 1995
  • Put Black Communities online in the mid-90s
  • Put Black Newspapers online since 2001
  • Built Technology Products for Fortune 100 Companies
  • Put the Government of a Caribbean Nation online in 2013
  • Hired dozens and Launched the Careers of Several Independent Black Technologists
  • Created the World's First and Largest Black History Encyclopedia in 1997
  • Created a Content Management and Syndication Platform that is 100% Black Conceived, Created, Coded and Owned
  • And more...

2021.title: Leveraging Social Media's 4 Billion Users
2021.subTitle: NNPA / Zenger News 2021 Conference
2021.description:
In this half-hour session at the National Newspaper Publishers Association / Zenger News 2021 Conference in February, BlackFacts.com CEO Dale Dowdie and CTO Ken Granderson share tips on how they organically grew and maintain a Social Media following of 200,000 for BlackFacts without external investors or staff – just some software tools and a part-time consultant.

We also describe how we are rebooting the Ethnic News Syndicate Platform we built that put Boston’s Bay State Banner online in 2001 to help grassroots and professional journalists, modern-day griots and other Truth-Tellers self-publish and syndicate their content across the globe for free or even at a profit.

2021.title: 26 Years of Diversity Technology Solutions
2021.subTitle: (Built on the Microsoft Stack)
2021.description:
This presentation done for a Microsoft engineering team showcases Diversity Technology Solutions we have created since 1995, built using tools and servers from Microsoft.

It also provides information on some behind-the-scenes things that Microsoft did to support and enable our Diversity Technology efforts, decades before it was trendy for companies to be viewed as 'Socially Conscious.'
2021.postscript: These are just PDF and PowerPoint shows - the video of the presentation is coming soon.

2021.title: Innovation Showcase TV (Newton, MA USA)
2021.subTitle: Innovation Showcase features and highlights a range of groundbreaking efforts throughout the state. The main purpose of this ongoing series is to inform viewers about exciting innovations and creative individuals across the fields of business, science, technology, education, and the arts.
2021.description:
In this half-hour interview, we show some of the pioneering work we did at the dawn of the Internet Age putting Communities of Color online since 1996, why we created BlackFacts, the world's First Online Black History Encyclopedia, and how we have evolved it into an advanced content aggregation, classification and syndication system that stands alone in the space of Technology created By Us, For Us, About Us, and Owned By Us.

We also share our vision of using our technology platform to power Black schools, organizations and businesses across the Diaspora.
Hosted by Jay Sugarman of https://newtv.org
'Jay talks with Ken Granderson and Dale Dowdie. Ken and Dale are the founders of BlackFacts.com, an extensive platform for information about Black history and culture. Ken serves as the Chief Technology Officer and Dale is the CEO.
During the program, we’ll be learning why and how BlackFacts.com came about and how it’s grown, developed, and operates today.
We’ll go on a behind-the-scenes tour, and, in the process, come to better understand and appreciate the breadth and depth of the site’s resources and information.'

2021.title: Ethics in AI - Just Because We CAN, Does It Mean We SHOULD?
2021.subTitle: A Panel Discussion on AI Ethics, Conducted During of Silicon Harlem's Annual Conference'
2021.description: Two years before the arrival of Generative AI for the masses, I conducted this panel of AI, Ethics and Technology experts on concerns and challenges and opportunities from the emergence of AI. Panelists were Reneé Cummings, AI expert and data scientist out of the University of Virginia who focuses on the impact of AI for underserved communities, Humanist Chaplain, President of Harvard Chaplains and New York Times bestselling author Greg Epstein, and David Ryan Polgar, founder and executive director of All Tech is Human an international organization of thousands of individuals committed to using technology for good.
